summary: Post-market 2026-11-02: the risk score of 66.45 is a new high for the observed window, holding high_risk with the regime flipping to risk_off for the first time — triggered by breadth (0.3355 of constituents above their 200-day average, through the 0.35 gate), not by VIX (19.42, still far below 28). The session was a narrow de-rating: 16 of 22 sector and theme rows fell and 6 rose, with an average decline of 2.2204 percent; networking fell 6.6295 percent, AI infrastructure 6.0846 percent (down 26.0042 percent over the month), AMD 7.5198 percent and MU 5.7814 percent, while the Dow rose 0.41 percent, fintech 1.8258 percent and Tesla 1.003 percent, and both Apple and Palantir beat consensus. Two forces lifted the score: breadth kept deteriorating (61 new lows against 42 on 10-30), and 10-30's credit and volatility prints entered the model only tonight (HY OAS 3.44, VIX 19.42), which alone added 2.5795 points, about 69 percent of the +3.75 move. Read plainly, this is a valuation clearing in the leadership block, not a liquidity event: the fragile point is breadth, and breadth is already below the gate.

top_risk_drivers.claim: Cross-asset confirmation held at 0.75 and contributed 11.25 points, the heaviest single block in the model: 6 of 8 scoring signals triggered, spanning the equity decline, dollar strength, real-rate pressure, bitcoin weakness, small-cap underperformance and gold strength. This is multi-point confirmation rather than one noisy leg.

High-yield OAS widened from 3.26 to 3.44, at the 87.88th percentile of its own history, contributing 7.0304 points; investment-grade OAS rose from 0.89 to 0.94, a risk score of 77.14. Credit is widening, but the absolute level stays below the 4.0 trigger, so that leg has not fired.

VIX rose from 17.20 to 19.42, a dimension risk score of 63.81 and a 5.1048-point contribution. The level is still low, far from the 28 volatility gate for risk_off, but it lifted the volatility dimension from 32.41 to 41.14.

The share of constituents above their 200-day average fell to 0.3355 (52 of 155), a dimension risk score of 81.45 and a 4.9578-point contribution; 61 names printed new lows, a ratio of 0.3885, the highest in the observed window. Breadth is the direct trigger of today's regime flip.

The 10-year real rate sits at 2.60, in the 97.43rd percentile, contributing 4.8715 points; the nominal 10-year is 4.94, below the prior 4.98. The long end eased slightly, but the real rate remains in an extreme range and keeps discounting long-duration growth stocks.

supporting_signals.claim: Semis relative strength (63-session basis) is -13.8401, nearly double the -6.8672 recorded on 10-30, with a dimension risk score of 80.12; the AI infrastructure theme fell another 6.0846 percent today. The underperformance is cumulative, not single-day noise.
The new-low ratio jumped from 0.2675 to 0.3885 while the new-high ratio is only 0.0318 (5 of 157). Declines are broadening faster than advances, the classic shape of a risk-appetite turn.

Networking fell 6.6295 percent, AI infrastructure 6.0846 percent, quantum computing 4.6482 percent and cybersecurity 4.2364 percent: the damage is concentrated in compute and connectivity, not spread evenly across the market.

contradicting_signals.claim: Realized volatility is only 11.3068 with a dimension risk score of 15.23, the healthiest of the six dimensions. A genuine systemic deleveraging would be unlikely to leave this reading near 11.

Internals were not uniformly negative: fintech rose 1.8258 percent, industrial automation 1.3951 percent, the EV supply chain 1.3538 percent and digital advertising 0.8052 percent, with 6 of the 22 rows positive.

The yield curve is 0.38, still positively sloped, with a dimension risk score of 34.40, and the new-high ratio at 0.0318 is above the 0.0127 of 10-30. Neither the curve nor the new-high count supports an imminent-recession read.

what_changed_today: The total score is 66.45, up 3.52 from the previous session (62.93 on 10-30) and up 3.75 from this morning's pre-market 62.70; the regime jumped from risk_on to risk_off, the first such reading in the observed window.
Breadth deteriorated further: the share above their 200-day average is 0.3355 against 0.3613 on 10-30, and new lows number 61 against 42.

The 10-30 credit and volatility prints entered the model only tonight: HY OAS 3.26 to 3.44, IG OAS 0.89 to 0.94 and VIX 17.20 to 19.42 lifted the score by 2.5795 points, about 69 percent of the +3.75 move.

AI and semis led the decline again: AMD fell 7.5198 percent, MU 5.7814 percent, the four-name semis basket 3.9357 percent and the Philadelphia semiconductor index more than 3 percent, while money rotated into fintech (1.8258 percent), industrial automation (1.3951 percent) and Tesla (1.003 percent).

Crude fell more than 7 percent as expectations of a US-Iran deal built, with Trump saying he will not strike Iran after the midterms. That is a tailwind for inflation and a headwind for energy equities.

Data-basis note: the A-share block still carries the previous settled session's (10-30) closes and changes because the upstream close is missing, so it is not today's A-share performance; the memory theme therefore covers only 6 of its 13 constituents.
watch_next: AMD reports tomorrow (11-03) with consensus EPS of 1.95; it fell 7.5198 percent today, and this print is the first gate for whether the semis chain stabilises.
Apple's first session after results: fiscal fourth-quarter EPS came in at 2.10 against a 2.00 consensus. Whether the AI narrative holds will be settled by tomorrow's pricing.

US midterm election day (11-03). Prediction markets put Democratic control of the Senate near 74 percent; sector-level policy sensitivity (healthcare, defense, crypto, AI regulation) matters more than the index level.
Whether breadth repairs: 0.3355 sits just 0.0145 below the 0.35 regime gate; if new lows keep expanding beyond 61 names, risk_off reinforces itself.

The data calendar: JOLTS job openings at 15:00Z tomorrow, the Employment Situation on 11-06 and CPI on 11-10. The monthly inflation series still sits at its previous print, with CPI at 3.71725 and core PCE at 3.12116, so the next repricing waits on new data.

Long-end supply and financing mix: the Treasury raised its quarterly borrowing estimate ahead of the refunding statement, while Oracle filed a large stock and bond sale and Meta plans its first euro bond. AI capex shifting from free cash flow to debt is a new pressure point for the long end and for credit.

bull_case.title: Bull case: a narrow de-rating, not a broad risk event
points: The Dow rose 0.41 percent against the tape, 6 of 22 rows were positive, and fintech rose 1.8258 percent with industrial automation up 1.3951 percent; money is rotating rather than leaving.
Realized volatility at 11.3068 (risk score 15.23), VIX at 19.42 and HY OAS at 3.44 are all far from stress territory, with a wide gap to the crisis thresholds of VIX 40 and HY OAS 7.0.
Fundamentals still score: Apple's fiscal fourth-quarter EPS of 2.10 beat consensus, Palantir grew revenue 96 percent and raised guidance, and Roku posted EPS of 1.20 against a 0.57 estimate.

Crude down more than 7 percent is a tailwind for inflation, the curve at 0.38 is not inverted, and neither copper (+1.2232) nor the cyclicals-versus-defensives ratio (+0.8326) has triggered, so evidence of a growth scare is thin.

base_case.title: Base case: narrow clearing, index holds, breadth decides the regime
points: The AI and semis de-rating continues but stays confined to the compute chain: AI infrastructure fell 6.0846 percent today and semiconductor equipment 3.7635 percent, while fintech rose 1.8258 percent and still sits in the 70.6th percentile of its one-year range.
The regime stays risk_off until the share above their 200-day average recovers above 0.35; it is 0.3355 now, just 0.0145 short.
Tomorrow's pricing hinges on two events: AMD's results (consensus EPS of 1.95) and Apple's first post-results session. If both hold, index-level losses keep running smaller than theme-level losses.

bear_case.title: Bear case: breadth failure, wider credit, heavier supply
points: At 61 names (ratio 0.3885) new lows are the highest in the observed window and only 0.3355 of constituents remain above their 200-day average; if breadth keeps sliding, the regime debate moves from risk_off to crisis.

Credit has widened for two straight weeks: HY OAS from 3.14 to 3.26 to 3.44 and IG from 0.86 to 0.89 to 0.94, while VIX ran 16.91 to 17.20 to 19.42 over the same stretch. All three move the same way, so pressure is accumulating rather than isolated.
The real rate sits at 2.60, in the 97.43rd percentile, with the 10-year at 4.94; debt-funded AI capex on top of heavy Treasury long-end supply keeps valuation pressure in place.
If AMD disappoints, the semis chain (semiconductor equipment already down 3.7635 percent today) faces a second de-rating leg, and the score would rise far faster than it did today.
